title: GRPO from Scratch
summary: GRPO is PPO without the value head: sample a group of completions per prompt, use their average reward as the baseline, and give every token of a completion the same advantage. This lesson reads the plain-PyTorch version in part_9 of the companion repo line by line, including how its KL term and batch normalisation differ from the paper and the library.
objectives: Explain why the group mean can replace PPO's learned value as a baseline, and estimate the memory that saves at small and large scale
Compute group-normalised advantages for a batch by hand and say how part_9's batch-level scaling and token-level re-centring change them
Trace how one advantage per completion is broadcast to every response token through act_mask and traj_id_for_token
Compare the k1 and k3 KL estimators and explain why a KL term added to the loss behaves differently from one folded into the reward
Instrument the training loop with reward, within-group spread and KL, and map each part_9 setting onto TRL's GRPOTrainer
prerequisites: This lesson changes the PPO loop from [RLHF with PPO](/learn/post-training/rlhf-with-ppo), which uses the reward model from [Reward models](/learn/post-training/reward-models); read those first. The theory is in [Verifiable rewards and group-relative advantages](/learn/fine-tuning/preference-tuning/verifiable-rewards-grpo), and the library version is [GRPO hands-on](/learn/fine-tuning/grpo-hands-on).
